speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please sit down and tell me what specific symptoms you, or your wife, have noticed since you arrived at the clinic today?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To clarify the timeline of his psychotic symptoms, how long ago did the delusions about the NSA and mind control first begin, and have there been any episodes of hallucinations?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia, paranoid type.

The patient presents with a 6-week history of persecutory delusions regarding mind control and surveillance, accompanied by agitated behavior and social withdrawal. The onset of these psychotic symptoms appears to coincide with his unemployment, and he has been constructing a delusional system involving the creation of a device to counteract the perceived conspiracy. This clinical picture, in the absence of a prior significant mood episode, strongly points toward a primary psychotic disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features.
